statement: 311 noise complaint rates by census tract are a poor measure of noise exposure: they align weakly with modelled transportation noise and more strongly with neighbourhood change (rent increase and growth of the non-Hispanic white share).

graph_evidence.summary: Road traffic noise and hypertension; e.g. OR 1.11 per 10 dB(A) (1.00-1.23) (PMID 24952459); incident hypertension RR 1.13 (1.02-1.24) in ESCAPE cohorts (PMID 28417138).
Traffic noise and stroke (count from the relationship record).
High road traffic noise and poorer sleep health OR 1.13 (1.06-1.20) (PMID 35513113).
Aircraft plus road noise >=45 dB: incident hypertension HR 1.39 (1.14-1.70) (PMID 30078646).

graph_evidence.note: The graph holds no finding on noise complaints as a measure. The research evidence is on measured or modelled dB, so the conflict is about whether the city's common proxy measures the research exposure.

literature.citation: Legewie J, Schaeffer M. Contested boundaries: explaining where ethnoracial diversity provokes neighborhood conflict. Am J Sociol 2016;122(1):125-61.
literature.finding: NYC 311 neighbour complaints (loud music, parties) are about 26% higher at fuzzy ethnoracial boundaries than in homogeneous areas or at sharp boundaries.

literature.citation: Kontokosta CE, Hong B. Bias in smart city governance: how socio-spatial disparities in 311 complaint behavior impact the fairness of data-driven decisions. Sustain Cities Soc 2021;64:102503.
literature.finding: 311 reporting propensity differs by income, race and tenure in NYC.

literature.citation: Estimating reporting bias in 311 complaint data. Ann Appl Stat 2025.
literature.finding: Reporting rates for the same underlying incident vary across NYC neighbourhoods.

literature.citation: Zheng Y, Liu T, Wang Y, et al. Diagnosing New York City's noises with ubiquitous data. UbiComp 2014.
literature.finding: Uses 311 noise complaints as the target for inferring noise, i.e. treats complaints as a measure.

literature.citation: Bello JP, Silva C, Nov O, et al. SONYC: a system for monitoring, analyzing, and mitigating urban noise pollution. Commun ACM 2019;62(2):68-77.
literature.finding: Sensor network in NYC; argues complaints are an incomplete signal of noise.

literature.citation: NY State Comptroller. Silencing excessive NYC noise (2018).
literature.finding: 311 noise complaints rose from about 200,000 (2010) to 384,000 (2015); few complaints are measured.

prediction.magnitude: In a joint OLS of log(1 + residential noise complaints per 1,000 residents, 2022-2024) on standardised predictors with borough fixed effects, the coefficient on rent change (ACS 2008-12 to 2018-22) exceeds the coefficient on modelled transportation noise by 0.05-0.30 log units per SD. Spearman rho between residential complaint rate and modelled noise below 0.25. Street/vehicle complaints show a positive association with modelled noise (rho 0.15-0.45).
prediction.support_if: The difference (rent-change coefficient minus modelled-noise coefficient) has a bootstrap 95% CI above 0.
prediction.refute_if: The difference has a 95% CI below 0 (complaints track modelled noise more than change): contested. Spanning 0: unsettled.

plan: Unit: 2020 census tracts with at least 500 residents. Complaints: 311 Service Requests 2020-present (erm2-nwe9), created 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31, complaint_type 'Noise - Residential' (primary), also 'Noise - Street/Sidewalk' + 'Noise - Vehicle', 'Noise - Commercial', and all types beginning 'Noise'; aggregated with SoQL group by latitude, longitude and complaint_type, then joined to tracts locally. Modelled noise: US DOT/BTS National Transportation Noise Map 2020, road+aviation+rail LAeq 24h, read from the geo.dot.gov tile service (classes 45-50, 50-55, 55-60, 60-70, 70-80, 80-90, >90 dB) and summarised as tract-mean class midpoint (below 45 dB set to 40) and share of area >=60 dB. Nightlife: active on-premises liquor licences per tract (NY State Liquor Authority data, data.ny.gov). Neighbourhood change: change in median gross rent (B25064, inflation not adjusted, in log) and in non-Hispanic white share (B03002) from ACS 2008-2012 (2010 tracts, area-weighted to 2020 tracts with the Census relationship file) to ACS 2018-2022. Controls: log population density, poverty share, borough fixed effects. Bootstrap tracts (1,000 draws) for the coefficient difference. SONYC sensor data used only if a public levels file is found; otherwise noted as unavailable. Figure: tract maps of complaint rate and modelled noise; coefficient plot with the research dose-response (per 10 dB) noted beside it.
alternatives: Residential complaints concern neighbour noise, which the transport noise map does not model; a weak link to modelled noise is then expected even if complaints measure exposure to their own source.
Rent change and nightlife are collinear (new bars follow rising rents); the rent coefficient may carry real noise from new venues.
Population density drives both complaints and actual neighbour noise.
The noise map is coarse (classes, no values under 45 dB) and models traffic volume, not observed levels.
Reporting propensity differs by language, trust in government and tenure, independent of change.
